title: A SIM-swap fraud model update locks out legitimate customers
summary: OpCo deploys version 2 of its fraud model for SIM-replacement requests. It blocks known fraud but also refuses many legitimate prepaid and roaming customers, who then cannot receive banking one-time passcodes.
precedent_note: Grounded in FCC 23-95 (which warns against delaying legitimate SIM changes), ACMA identity-verification penalties 2025-2026 and India's automated SIM re-verification. No regulator has yet found a telco fraud model locking out users at scale; the false-positive harm rests on rule text and adjacent cases.

injects.text: Fraud model v2 went live for SIM-replacement requests at 08:00. The fraud dashboard shows refused SIM replacements up about tenfold and labels it a 'fraud wave'.
Several banks report that customers who are abroad cannot receive one-time passcodes and are locked out of online banking. The customers say OpCo refused their SIM replacement requests.

Analysis of v2: refusals concentrate on prepaid and roaming customer profiles. About 2,750 legitimate requests have been refused since 08:00 (synthetic data). Known fraud is still blocked. There is no human review path for a refused request.

injects.label: Day 2
injects.text: A customer group complains that 'automated decisions' refused their SIM replacement with no explanation and no way to appeal.

injects.label: Day 2
injects.text: Internal question to the regulator's duty officer: which UAE instrument sets the authentication requirements an operator must apply to SIM-swap requests?

debrief: The exercise is ending. Using only the KNOWLEDGE excerpts, record the obligations that applied to you, the coordination problems you saw, and the policy gaps this incident exposed, each with a global example where one exists. Take any final actions.

duties.description: Restore service for legitimate customers without letting fraud through
Give bank-flagged customers a non-SMS confirmation route
Coordinate the operator and banking sides
Provide human review of automated decisions on request
Data authority asks for the human-review record
